articleSummary: Invasive meningococcal disease (Neisseria meningitidis) can affect healthy people, with adolescents and young adults at higher risk, especially in dormitories, boarding schools, or military barracks. It often begins with flu-like symptoms but can rapidly progress to meningitis or septicemia, risking death. Transmission occurs via respiratory secretions during close contact; asymptomatic carriers can spread the bacteria. Early signs include fever, headache, myalgia, nausea, and vomiting; progression may cause meningitis, septic shock, disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), multi-organ failure, and death. CDC notes about 10-15% mortality despite antibiotics; roughly 20% of survivors have long-term sequelae such as hearing loss or brain injury. Vaccines MenACWY (A, C, W, Y) and MenB (group B) protect against different serogroups; vaccination should be planned before crowded living settings. To reduce risk: avoid sharing utensils, wash hands, ventilate spaces, and avoid smoking. Close contacts may require antibiotic prophylaxis; vaccination does not replace this.

articleHeadline: Simple Blood Ratio Could Flag Severe Influenza Before Treatment Begins
articleSummary: Pre-treatment neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR) from routine CBCs differentiates severe from non-severe influenza in adults. In a retrospective study of 1,091 laboratory-confirmed influenza A or B cases admitted to Guangdong Second Provincial General Hospital (2016–2023), higher NPR before treatment predicted severe disease; NPR decreased after therapy (P=0.012 for influenza A; P=0.028 for influenza B). NPR correlated positively with interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels (P<0.0001), linking NPR to the inflammatory state driving severity. Logistic regression identified pre-treatment NPR as an independent predictor of severe influenza (P=0.001 for A; P<0.0001 for B). Combining NPR with lymphocyte count improved discrimination between influenza patients and healthy individuals (P<0.05). Implications: NPR could serve as a rapid, cost-free triage biomarker in fever clinics and emergency departments to guide monitoring and antiviral treatment decisions.

articleSummary: Streptococcus suis, a zoonotic pathogen affecting pigs and humans, is studied by a Henan University of Science and Technology team in China. They show that the anticancer drug 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) can markedly weaken S. suis biofilm formation and virulence at subinhibitory concentrations, without killing bacteria. 5-FU loosens biofilms, reduces extracellular and capsule polysaccharide synthesis, and downregulates virulence genes, lowering adhesion and resistance to phagocytosis. articleHeadline: Resistant bacterial and fungal infections linked to COVID-19 mortality
articleSummary: Resistant bacterial and fungal infections among adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 were linked to substantially higher in-hospital mortality in a single-center Chinese study (Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine; Nov 2022–Feb 2023). Of 428 inpatients with microbiological data, 333 (77.8%) developed at least one additional infection. Co-infection was detected within 48 hours of admission; secondary infection occurred after 48 hours. Pathogens were grouped into Gram-negative, Gram-positive bacteria and fungi, with resistant isolates tracked separately. Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (55.9% of infections) and resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (38.4%) were most common, followed by fungi (33.0%) and resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (14.1%). Four trajectories were analyzed: no infection; sensitive-bacterial infection; resistant-bacterial infection; and fungal involvement. Mortality was 22.1%, 55.1%, 60.9%, and 64.9% across these groups. Adjusted odds ratios vs no infection: 2.87 (sensitive bacteria), 3.15 (fungal), 4.69 (resistant bacteria). Sensitivity analyses (propensity-score matching OR 2.05; IPTW OR 4.13) supported associations; time-dependent analyses showed higher death hazard with infection. Limitations include single-center, retrospective design and potential confounding.

articleSummary: Newcastle disease outbreak in Brazil prompts Mexico’s Senasica to suspend imports of avian-origin products. Mexican authorities confirmed Newcastle disease at a commercial broiler farm in Nova Itaberaba, Santa Catarina, prompting a precautionary halt on Brazilian poultry shipments. Mexico, which maintains Newcastle disease-free status, aims to protect its domestic poultry sector. As part of preventive actions, Senasica’s General Directorate of Animal Health deactivated the Zoosanitary Requirements Sheets in its platform, blocking entry of various avian products until zoosanitary information on Brazil’s outbreak is reviewed. The suspension covers poultry meat, offal, cage birds and ornamental birds, as well as avian genetic material including fertile eggs and day-old chicks up to three days old. The restriction applies to both commercial imports and poultry products carried by travelers, and will be maintained in line with international protocols while Brazil addresses the outbreak.
notes: 本事案は家禽の動物疾病（ニューカッスル病）に関するものであり、ヒトの公衆衛生リスクとしての評価対象ではなく、家禽産業・貿易分野の事案として扱うべき。メキシコは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsには含めない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Aedes aegypti's cousin lays eggs more than 10 meters off the ground.
articleHeadline: Primo do Aedes aegypti põe ovos a mais de 10 metros do solo
articleSummary: Eggs of Aedes albopictus were found on all levels of a six-story Manaus tower (Amazonas, Brazil), up to 10.8 meters, using 30 ovitraps. Most eggs clustered near ground (up to ~4 m), but occurrences on every floor suggest high-rise residents may face exposure to arboviruses. Aedes albopictus, a relative of Aedes aegypti, can transmit dengue, Zika, chikungunya, and yellow fever, though Brazil has no documented dengue transmission by this species. Natural dengue infection has been identified in this species; lab tests show transmission capacity, but not proven in natural conditions. Dry-season humidity explained 34% of egg abundance; in the rainy season, humidity, temperature, and rainfall were not significant. Experts urge expanding surveillance to upper floors in urban buildings; how mosquitoes reach higher levels remains unclear—flight or passive transport via elevators or people. In Ceará, 15,400 dengue cases were reported in the first 40 epidemiological weeks of 2026.
notes: 記事は媒介蚊の生態研究が主題であり、ブラジルにおけるこの種によるデング熱等の自然感染伝播は未確認。セアラ州のデング熱症例数（15,400件）は参考情報として言及されているが、本記事の主眼は昆虫学的調査結果。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Exposure to a child with meningococcal disease for several days: are prophylactic antibiotics still timely?
articleHeadline: Tiếp xúc trẻ mắc não mô cầu đã vài ngày, uống kháng sinh dự phòng còn kịp?
articleSummary: Prophylactic antibiotics for close contacts of meningococcal disease are most effective when started promptly, ideally within 24 hours of case confirmation, according to Dr. Nguyen Minh Tien, Deputy Director of City Children's Hospital in Ho Chi Minh City. If 2–3 days have passed, parents should still seek medical assessment rather than assume prophylaxis is unnecessary. After about 14 days from illness onset, the benefit is generally limited; final decisions depend on physician and public health officials. Per Ministry of Health guidance, close contacts—household members, roommates, direct care workers, and classmates who had contact from 7 days before onset to 24 hours after the patient received antibiotics—should be monitored and offered prevention measures. Vaccination, personal hygiene, and healthy habits are emphasized; seek hospital care promptly if meningococcal symptoms appear.
notes: 記事は髄膜炎菌感染症の濃厚接触者への予防的抗生物質投与に関する医学的アドバイス記事であり、特定のアウトブレイクの報告ではない。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Mexico bans the import of chicken and poultry products from Brazil due to Newcastle disease.
articleHeadline: México prohíbe ingreso de pollo y productos avícolas de Brasil por Newcastle
articleSummary: Mexico bans the import of chicken, fertile eggs, live birds, and poultry products carried by travelers from Brazil after Newcastle disease was confirmed at a commercial turkey farm in Nova Itaberaba, Santa Catarina. The outbreak was confirmed Oct 18, 2026, in a farm of about 6,000 turkeys; samples were taken between Sept 21 and Oct 14, 2026. Brazil immobilized the farm, halted bird movements, and ordered culling with cleaning and disinfection. A surveillance zone covering roughly 133 properties in Nova Itaberaba and nearby Coronel Freitas, Nova Erechim, and Águas Frias was established. The ban, announced Oct 19 by Mexico’s Secretariat of Agriculture and Senasica, aims to protect an Newcastle-free Mexico by suspending zoosanitary requirements for affected goods. Newcastle is a viral disease in poultry with respiratory, digestive, and nervous signs; human infections are rare. Mexico previously restricted Brazilian poultry during the 2025 H5N1 avian influenza outbreak.
notes: 本事例はニューカッスル病（家禽の疾病）であり人獣共通感染症としてのヒトへの健康影響は記載されていない。メキシコは対象国リストに含まれないため、発生国であるブラジルのみを記載。
